name: Monaco
summary: Children are protected by a reserved share that a will cannot remove, but a person can choose their national law under the 2017 reform. Monaco has had the Hague Trusts Convention in force since 2008. Its own trust-like and foundation tools are narrow.
reserved_share: Children are protected by a reserve under the Civil Code and the 2017 reform kept it. The fractions were not confirmed from a primary source.
foreign_law_note: Law 1.448 of 28 June 2017: one law, that of the deceased's domicile at death, applies to the whole estate; a person may choose their national law for the whole estate (professio juris). Not under the EU Regulation.
trust_note: The Hague Trusts Convention is in force since 1 September 2008 (HCCH table: accession 1 June 2007), and Law 1.448 clarifies recognition of foreign trusts. Domestic law offers a narrow fiducie (Law 214 of 1936) and foundations (Law 56 of 1922) for public-interest purposes; neither was read in detail.
open_questions: Fractions of the Monegasque reserve were not sourced.
Law 214 (fiducie) and the foundation law were identified from secondary text only; their scope was not confirmed.
Whether a choice of national law defeats the reserve for children who are Monegasque residents was not confirmed.
